findings.body:
**Authentication bypass:** `identity()` now decodes JWTs with `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` all set to `False`, and no key or algorithm is supplied.

Anyone who can send a request can forge a token with an arbitrary payload (any `sub`, roles, tenant, etc.) and this function will treat it as valid. The comment references staging re-issuance (TICKET-412), but there is no environment, config flag, or build-time guard limiting the bypass to staging — whatever deploys this file is wide open.

Restoring verification is the fix. If staging tokens use a new signing key after the accounts migration, pass that key (or a short allowlist of keys) into `jwt.decode` and keep `algorithms=["HS256"]`, `audience="api"`, and `issuer` (or an explicit issuer allowlist). Do not ship `verify_signature: False` on a shared code path.

```suggestion
    return jwt.decode(
        token,
        SECRET,
        algorithms=["HS256"],
        audience="api",
        issuer="accounts.internal.example",
    )
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification in `identity()`, which is a full authentication bypass: any client can mint an unsigned token and impersonate any principal.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` accepts any well-formed JWT payload with no cryptographic check. The comment cites staging token re-issuance (TICKET-412), but nothing in the function (or surrounding module) gates the bypass to a non-production environment. If this module is deployed as-is, production inherits the same hole.

The previous call verified `HS256` with `SECRET`, `audience="api"`, and `issuer="accounts.internal.example"`. Those checks are load-bearing; removing them is not a temporary staging convenience unless the binary that ships them cannot reach prod.

## Safer direction

Keep verification on. If staging tokens were signed with a rotated key, configure the new key (or a dual-key accept list) and keep `algorithms`, `audience`, and `issuer`. If old and new issuers must overlap briefly, verify against an explicit allowlist of keys/issuers rather than turning verification off.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: auth.py identity() now calls jwt.decode with verify_signature, verify_aud, and verify_iss all False and no key/algorithms; the prior version verified with SECRET, HS256, audience, and issuer. There is no staging/env guard, so forged tokens are accepted on this shared path.
